Robot maker Northwind will pay $4.2 billion for its sensor supplier

SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Northwind Robotics, whose self-driving forklifts move pallets in warehouses across North America, is buying the company that makes the eyes for its machines.

The San Jose-based firm announced Wednesday that it will acquire Contoso Sensors in an all-cash deal worth roughly $4.2 billion, or $38 a share. Contoso stockholders still have to sign off, as do antitrust regulators in the U.S. and Europe.

Industry watchers have long noted how dependent Northwind is on a single supplier. Contoso provides the lidar units and depth cameras that let Northwind robots see shelves, people and other vehicles, and the two companies have worked together since 2017.

Maria Alvarez, Northwind's chief executive, framed the purchase as a way to protect its margins and speed up development. She told investors the combined company could trim what it spends on parts by around an eighth over the next couple of years.

Contoso's stock surged in early trading Wednesday. Northwind's dipped slightly as investors weighed the roughly $1.5 billion in borrowing the company plans to take on to help pay for the deal.

Northwind expects the purchase to be completed by mid-2027.

Associated Press writer Dana Park in New York contributed to this report.
